exposure: Sonographic signs (large lacunae, loss of clear zone)
Placental location (major or minor placenta praevia)
outcome: Placenta accreta spectrum (PAS) condition at delivery
cohort: The study included 481 women with singleton pregnancies at 28 weeks or later, who had a scarred uterus or placenta praevia and underwent sonographic testing for PAS detection between 2010 and 2020.
finding: A screening model combining placental location and at least one sonographic sign demonstrated high sensitivity (94.9%) and specificity (91.5%) for prenatal prediction of placenta accreta spectrum.
